fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Mark the entrance to each detached structure with a visible identifier so responders can distinguish between buildings on arrival.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach all structures without obstruction.
• Identify and mark a designated turnaround point near the end of the access drive so responders do not have to back out blind.
• Clear vegetation along both sides of the access drive to allow full-width vehicle passage without obstruction.
• Trim any vegetation that blocks sightlines between the main residence and detached structures.
• Keep a clear foot path between all structures so responders can move on foot without pushing through vegetation.
• Mark all secondary access points to the property so responders can quickly locate alternate entry routes.
• Keep gates on secondary access points unlocked or secured with a method accessible to emergency responders.
• Keep the storage area and equipment storage area accessible from at least one side so responders can assess and reach those areas quickly.
• Remove stored materials from areas immediately adjacent to structures that would block responder movement around building perimeters.
• Post a simple site map near the primary driveway entrance showing the location of all structures, parking areas, and access points.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang over or touch the house and any outbuildings.
• Thin scattered trees near structures so individual tree canopies do not touch each other.
• Mow or cut grass growing close to the house and any outbuildings before it dries out seasonally.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or within a few feet of any structure.
• Separate shrubs from nearby trees so vegetation does not form a connected path toward structures.
• Clear dry grass and loose plant material from under parked vehicles and equipment stored in the open.
• Keep grass along the driveway cut short to reduce fire running along the edges toward the house.
